{{Quote|Lord Vader has also revised the targeting list. Have the operations people retarget probe droids for the planets Allyuen, Tokmia, and Hoth.|Captain Lorth Needa, Star Destroyer ''Avenger''|<ref name="ESB NPR" />}}
'''Tokmia''' was a mostly [[Water/Legends|icy]], snow-covered [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Home to the primitive, barely-[[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Oku]] [[Species/Legends|species]], Tokmia featured bountiful [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] and [[Ore/Legends|ore]] deposits, from which the [[Figg Excavations/Legends|Figg Excavations]] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] company earned a fortune before abandoning the planet. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Tokmia was one of three worlds in the Anoat [[Sector/Legends|sector]], including [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], to which the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] sent reconnaissance [[Viper probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] in search of the hidden [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Alliance High Command/Legends|base]].

==Description==
Tokmia was a [[Temperature/Legends|frigid]], frozen tundra [[Planet/Legends|world]] covered with vast flatlands of [[Water/Legends|snow]] and ice,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|252|Tokmia}}</ref> as well as lush [[Forest/Legends|forests]] and [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]].<ref name="Rebellion" /> The planet was located in the [[Tokmia system/Legends|Tokmia system]] of the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]], within the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']]<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" /> [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]].<ref name="Atlas" /> It was positioned at the virtual center of the Anoat [[Sector/Legends|sector]], at the terminus of a minor [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] connected to the major [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]] by way of the [[Ione system/Legends|Ione system]].<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

Tokmia numbered among a cluster of three other nearby, similarly [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]]-rich planets&mdash;[[Burnin Konn/Legends|Burnin Konn]], [[Allyuen/Legends|Allyuen]], and [[Isis/Legends|Isis]]&mdash;collectively known as the [[Mining Worlds/Legends|Mining Worlds]].<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" /> Tokmia boasted rich [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] and [[Ore/Legends|ore]] deposits, an enticing draw for [[Mining/Legends|mining]] prospects.<ref name="CSWE" /> A [[Standard day/Legends|day]] on Tokmia lasted eighteen [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard hours]], and a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] 220 local days. The planet had 90 percent standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] and a Type I [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] breathable for [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

==History==
===Mining operations===
[[Figg Excavations/Legends|Figg Excavations]], the mining subsidiary of the [[Outer Javin Company]], once turned Tokmia into a hugely lucrative [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]]-making venture by exploiting the planet's crystal and ore deposits.<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" /> The Tokmia mining enterprise earned Figg Excavations a fortune, and company employees distributed handouts to the planet's native [[Oku]] [[Species/Legends|species]] during each operation.<ref name="CSWE" /> Once the planet's mines ran dry, Figg Excavations pulled out and abandoned Tokmia, leaving behind a strange [[Oku cargo cult|cargo cult]] among the Oku, who, remembering the gifts they had been given, burned huge [[Fire/Legends|fires]] to resemble landing lights in prophesy that the [[Magic/Legends|magical]] [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of the offworlders would one day return.<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

===Search for the Rebel base===
[[File:ProbeDroidsMap-TEA.png|thumb|right|260px|This map shows the Imperial probe droids' launch trajectories, targeting Tokmia, Allyuen, and Hoth.]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date-Probe">According to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] dispatches [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] to Tokmia, [[Allyuen/Legends|Allyuen]], and [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] during the events of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]. {{CSWECite|III|45|probe droid (probot)}} identifies these probes as [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]].</ref> during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Tokmia briefly attracted the interest of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="ESB NPR">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> As part of his search for the hidden [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Alliance High Command/Legends|base]] following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Vader ordered<ref name="CSWE" /> his personal [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]], the [[Death Squadron/Legends|Imperial Death Squadron]],<ref name="Atlas" /> to dispatch reconnaissance [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]]<ref name="Date-Probe" /> to three planets in the Anoat sector to which the Empire suspected the Rebellion may have relocated: Tokmia, Allyuen, and [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="CSWE" />

The [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] and ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]'',<ref name="Atlas" /> the former under the command of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]],<ref name="ESB NPR" /> both sent out [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] assigned to the Tokmia [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Vader's directive to search Tokmia, Allyuen, and Hoth was a departure from the ''Avenger''{{'s}} original target schedule.<ref name="ESB NPR" /> The Empire ultimately discovered that Hoth was the planet hosting the Rebellion's new [[Echo Base/Legends|base]].<ref name="Atlas" />

==Inhabitants==
Tokmia was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of some 400,000 Oku, a barely-[[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], primitive species of [[Color/Legends|white]]-[[Hair/Legends|furred]] [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] who governed themselves in tribal councils. The abandonment of Figg Excavations' mining operation on Tokmia had a deeply profound impact on the Oku mythos, in which the Oku prophesied that their benevolent offworld visitors would return to their planet again.<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

==Locations==
Figg Excavations left behind an abandoned mining colony on Tokmia complete with a [[Spaceport/Legends|starport]] after exhausting the planet's crystal deposits and then moving on to other endeavors.<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

==Behind the scenes==
The planet Tokmia was first mentioned in the script for the [[1983]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], written by [[Brian Daley]]. Tokmia is one of three planets, Hoth included, to which Captain Needa of the Star Destroyer ''Avenger'' is assigned to send probe droids in search of the secret Rebel base.<ref name="ESB NPR" /> However, the dialogue portion of this scene that mentioned Tokmia was cut from the final version of the radio adaptation<ref name="ESB radio">[[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]]</ref> and appears only in the script's [[1995]] publication, ''[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization]]''.<ref name="ESB NPR" />

Tokmia was later one of 200 playable worlds included in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|PC game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], which provided the planet's only visual depiction, an image also used to illustrate twenty-one other planets of similar composition in the game. ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' described Tokmia as a lush forest planet,<ref name="Rebellion" /> but the [[2004]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] [[Wizards.com|online]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] supplement ''[[Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin]]'' described Tokmia as a snow-covered world, in the same vein as Hoth,<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" /> which was repeated by all subsequent sources detailing the planet.<ref name="Atlas" /><ref name="CSWE" /> In addition, ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' and its accompanying [[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] originally placed Tokmia in the [[Churba sector/Legends|Churba sector]],<ref name="Rebellion" /><ref name="Rebellion Prima's Official Strategy Guide">[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Rebellion'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> but ''Hoth and the Greater Javin'' changed its location to the Greater Javin region.<ref name="Galactic Gazetteer" />

===''Star Wars: Rebellion'' cartography===
''Star Wars: Rebellion'' provides [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel [[Time/Legends|times]] between each planet in the game. However, in several instances these times are significantly longer than those in other [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] sources, which seems to reflect the ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' hyperspace times as game mechanics rather than actual figures. Tokmia's intra-sector hyperspace times and distance from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] according to ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' using the game's fastest [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] are as follows. Note that this chart only includes planets that were [[canon]]ically located in the Anoat sector with respect to the Legends continuity, excepting Coruscant.
